en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha for the Tathāgata Mahātejas-cakravarti-uṣṇīṣa-jvalita-prabha to Eliminate All Calamities and Disasters;
Translated during the Tang Dynasty, Author Unknown.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha,
dwelling in the palace of the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven,
addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī.

As well as the fourfold assembly, the eight classes of beings, the great devas who roam the sky, the nine grahas, the seven luminaries, the deities of the twelve zodiacal mansions, the twenty-eight lunar mansions, the sun, the moon, and all the constellations:
in the past, at the abode of the Buddha King of Śāla Trees, I [made this vow].
Having received this Dharma of the *Dhāraṇī for Eliminating All Calamities* of the Tathāgata Great Majestic Virtue Golden Wheel Uṣṇīṣa Blazing Light,
if there should be any realm in future ages...
The sun, moon, five planets, Rāhu, Ketu, comets, meteors, and malevolent stars—
when these shine upon one’s natal mansion, the lunar mansions (nakṣatras), or various stellar positions;
or when they approach the imperial seat within the state, the family, or the specific regional domain (fenye).
When one is being oppressed or invaded, and various calamities arise,
one should establish a *maṇḍala* in a pure place and,
with a sincere mind, recite this *dhāraṇī* sūtra one hundred and eight times, or one thousand and eighty times.
If one practices the purification of the ritual site according to the Dharma for one day, two days, or even up to seven days, and maintains and recites [the mantra],
all calamities will naturally be extinguished and will be unable to cause harm.
If a great white fire-meteor enters the Southern Dipper (Nandou),
causing calamities and disasters for the state, the family, or the corresponding astrological division,
one should [perform rites] before an image of a wrathful deity.
Draw the form of that Śatadru and empower it by reciting this mantra;
the calamity will then immediately disperse and shift onto those who disobey the king’s commands and act in rebellion.
He then spoke the dhāraṇī mantra, saying:

*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām apratihataśāsanānām | Oṃ kha kha khahi khahi hūṃ hūṃ jvala jvala prajvala prajvala sthira sthira stambhaya stambhaya śāntika śrīye svāhā*. The Buddha said: "If, within the borders of a kingdom or a specific region, there be men or women..."
If one's physical form is afflicted by the influence of various devas or celestial bodies,
one should simply transcribe this sutra and wholeheartedly receive, uphold, read, and recite it,
always maintaining ritual purity.
This dhāraṇī was proclaimed by all Tathāgatas together;
it can accomplish eighty thousand kinds of great auspicious matters and can further eliminate eighty thousand kinds of great inauspicious matters.
If there are kings, ministers, their retinues, or any of the common people who are afflicted by the five planets,
Rāhu, Ketu, comets, meteors, or other malevolent and ominous constellations;
The imperial throne is encroached upon, whether in the state or the household, as well as in the specific fields, locations, palaces, and lunar mansions to which they belong;
calamities arise in competition.
Either Saturn invades and encroaches, or it advances, or it retreats.
Furthermore, when enemies from past lives seek to plot harm against one another,
or when various evil and calamitous events— such as verbal disputes, malevolent incantations, curses, and talismanic scripts— are used to bring about disaster,
it causes all sentient beings to receive and uphold [this teaching] according to the Dharma.
No calamities whatsoever can cause harm;
they transform misfortunes into blessings, and all attain auspiciousness.
I declare that the inconceivable merit of this mantra is peerless.
Hold this in secret and do not proclaim it recklessly.
The Buddha told the great assembly: "If there are times when a kingdom is unstable and calamities arise, or when men and women encounter misfortunes, disasters, and adversities..."
I only request that the assembly of monks establish a *maṇḍala* according to the Dharma, install the Buddha image, maintain pure precepts,
and provide offerings of incense, flowers, lamps, and candles as their means allow. By doing so,
all sentient beings will obtain immeasurable merit and their calamities shall be immediately eliminated.
At that time, the Tathāgata again addressed the great assembly:
"If a person’s birth year is afflicted by the five planets— Gold, Wood, Water, Fire, and Earth— or if Rāhu,
Ketu, the Sun, the Moon, or various lunar mansions descend upon their person."
Calamities arise in succession.
I possess a Great Auspicious Mantra called "Destroyer of Planets" (Bhasmagraha).
If one can receive and uphold it, recollecting it with a sincere mind, [these calamities shall be averted].
The calamities will extinguish themselves and misfortunes will be transformed into blessings.
Then he spoke this mantra:
Oṃ sarvanakṣatramātre śrīye śāntikā kuru svāhā. At that time, when the Tathāgata was preaching this sūtra...
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, along with the fourfold assembly,
the deities who roam the sky, the great gods, the various stars and constellations, and all the holy multitudes,
having all received the Buddha’s command, prostrated themselves, respectfully upheld it, and each returned to their own palace.
When the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were all greatly rejoiced;
they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The *Sūtra on the Radiant Light that Eliminates Calamities* Spoken by the Buddha contains the mantras of the nine planets as follows:

Gold: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ oṃ mahākhecarāya svāhā*. Wood: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ oṃ indrāya svāhā*. Water: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ oṃ varuṇāya svāhā*. Fire: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ oṃ agnaye svāhā*. Earth: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ oṃ pṛthivyai svāhā*. Rāhu: [Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ oṃ rāhave svāhā].

Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ raṇahūna asurāraya hūṃ svāhā | Ketu | Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ vajra ketunodghāṭarañjaya hūṃ svāhā | Sūrya | Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ aniṣṭya svāhā | Candra | Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ somaya svāhā |
